record.title: Tan Thanh–Po Chai halts Vietnamese cargo exports during COVID controls
record.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
record.scope: Vietnamese exports through Tan Thanh–Po Chai (Pu Zhai)
record.movement: Vietnam-to-China freight, including fresh agricultural produce.
record.exceptions: Imports into Vietnam and empty-vehicle returns were possible by December 22–23; not a total two-way border closure.
record.enforcement: Contemporary gate official and truckers describe halted exports; first three agricultural export vehicles cleared January 25.
record.relationship: Separate crossing from EA027 Dongxing and R2-EA-006 Hekou; related but not duplicate of three Chi Ma spells.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; unknown endpoints are not extended to 21 October 2026.
record.official_rationale: Strengthen COVID-19 prevention, according to MoIT account of Guangxi decision.
record.context: Earlier December 15 technical interruption is excluded; the new December 18 halt followed a short resumption.
record.uncertainty: Chinese reason was not initially announced to the local official; later ministry report supplies public-health attribution. Reopening remained low-capacity.

historical.duration_note: Calendar-date difference to the stated partial reopening for the specified movement and crossing; not exact hours or universal closure. Eligible only as the calendar gap to first documented Vietnamese agricultural-export passage on January 25; low-capacity partial resumption, not normalization or a two-way closure.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Contemporary local reporting distinguishes export stoppage from mere congestion.
December 18 restart then renewed suspension, consistently dated.
First-day report establishes three agricultural export vehicles on Jan 25, a partial operational reopening under restrictive clearance procedures.
